stories.body: Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the CDU’s performance a “disaster” after it fell below the 5% threshold in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where the far-right AfD was projected to finish first with about 38% of the vote. In Berlin, Die Linke was on course to lead with roughly 25%, ahead of the CDU on 19%, while the AfD also made gains. Merz, facing poor approval ratings and speculation about his future, said he would remain chancellor and CDU leader and press ahead with economic, tax, welfare and bureaucracy reforms; other parties are expected to maintain their refusal to govern with the AfD.
stories.headline: Germany’s CDU suffers heavy regional election losses as the far-right AfD advances

stories.body: Preliminary results from Russia’s first parliamentary election since the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine showed Vladimir Putin’s United Russia headed for another constitutional majority in the State Duma. With more than 90% of ballots counted, state-reported figures put the party at 57.86% of the vote, while the remaining parliamentary parties broadly support Kremlin policy. Anti-war opposition was heavily constrained: liberal Yabloko was removed from the party-list ballot and none of its individual candidates appeared set to win a seat. The Kremlin is likely to portray the result as public backing for Putin and the war despite economic strain, battlefield losses and recent Ukrainian attacks.
stories.headline: Putin’s United Russia retains a large parliamentary majority in tightly controlled wartime vote

stories.body: Senior US and Chinese officials discussed creating a notification or dialogue mechanism for serious artificial-intelligence incidents with national-security implications during talks in New York, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said. The talks, involving Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, were intended to prepare for a Washington summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping later this week and also covered trade issues ahead of the November expiry of a tariff truce. Both governments described the exchanges as constructive, while competing intensely for leadership in AI and other advanced technologies.
stories.headline: US and China discuss an AI-safety communication channel ahead of Trump-Xi summit

stories.body: Iran’s central military command said it had intelligence that the United States was preparing to resume strikes and warned that any new assault would bring retaliation against US bases and interests across the region. Donald Trump said he was considering military action, economic pressure or a deal and left open the possibility of meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the UN General Assembly. The confrontation follows renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi targets and is disrupting shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, while Qatar works to revive negotiations and Iranian officials signal both readiness for further fighting and openness to diplomacy.
stories.headline: Iran warns that the US may resume strikes as violence continues across the Middle East

stories.body: French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pledged closer cooperation on energy, climate, space and strategic autonomy during a meeting in Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, the French territory off Canada’s Atlantic coast. The symbolic visit came as Canada seeks stronger links with Europe amid an increasingly hostile trade relationship with the United States. Macron backed a proposed arrangement that could make Canada the EU’s first associate member, while Paris also hopes Canadian liquefied natural gas exports can help Europe diversify energy supplies.
stories.headline: Macron and Carney seek closer France-Canada ties amid strained relations with the United States

stories.body: An investigation by Forbidden Stories, France 24 and partner outlets reports that the Trump administration has deported more than 25,000 people since January 2025 to countries other than their own, often under little-publicized agreements. About 20,000 were sent to Mexico and more than 5,000 were flown to countries in Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean and Central Asia with which they had no connection. The reporting documents cases including an Iranian woman sent to the Central African Republic after having received legal protection in the US, and describes advocates’ concerns that people may subsequently be returned to countries where they face danger.
stories.headline: Investigation documents Trump administration deportations to third countries across Africa and Latin America

stories.body: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan DoorDash driver, in the torso during a traffic stop in Austin, Texas. He was reported to be in stable but serious condition and in ICE custody. The Department of Homeland Security said it was investigating, but details of what led to the shooting remain unclear. Mayor Kirk Watson, Austin police and local elected officials called for an independent inquiry and the release of body-camera footage, as protesters gathered at the scene demanding that ICE leave the city.
stories.headline: ICE officer shoots and wounds a man during a traffic stop in Austin, prompting protests

stories.body: The White House said Donald Trump will meet Emmanuel Macron in New York on Monday, before the opening of the UN General Assembly’s high-level week. The meeting brings together two leaders whose governments have recently faced disagreements over trade, geopolitical issues and international policy, while both are attending the annual gathering of world leaders.
stories.headline: Trump is set to meet Macron in New York as the UN General Assembly opens

stories.body: Madrid investigating judge Juan Carlos Peinado has ordered Begoña Gómez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, to stand trial on allegations of influence peddling and embezzlement linked to her university work and the use of a government adviser. Her adviser, Cristina Álvarez, will also face trial over an alleged role in the diversion of software developed through a Complutense University program. The case will be heard before a jury, though prosecutors still have to file their final position and have previously been expected to seek Gómez’s acquittal. The judge issued the order during his final week before retirement.
stories.headline: Judge orders Begoña Gómez to stand trial on alleged influence-peddling and embezzlement charges

stories.body: Spain’s government says up to 3,000 migrants, including an estimated 500 to 700 children, remain on Ceuta’s streets and beaches after a major influx, and plans to move them to suitable accommodation in the coming weeks. Ministers are urging the transfer of unaccompanied minors to mainland regions to ease pressure on the autonomous city, arguing that Spanish law requires individual procedures before any return and permits asylum claims and appeals. The government has accused the opposition Popular Party and Vox of promoting unrealistic claims of immediate returns, while Ceuta’s local authorities remain central to any relocation plan.
stories.headline: Ceuta’s migration crisis intensifies as authorities face pressure over shelter, asylum and the relocation of minors

stories.body: A crowd attacked the car of Ceuta Ya! assembly member Julia Ferreras at the city’s port, throwing stones and eggs and damaging the vehicle as she travelled with activist Rafael Borrego and human-rights lawyer Sofía Cánovas. The protesters had gathered over the expected arrival of a Navarra-based housing and aid group and apparently targeted Ferreras’s vehicle despite its lack of connection to the organization. Ferreras said anti-migrant rhetoric following the mass arrivals in Ceuta had fuelled hostility and fear; Spain’s government and Ceuta’s authorities condemned the attack.
stories.headline: Attack on a Ceuta assembly member’s car highlights escalating tensions around the migration crisis

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is traveling to New York for the UN General Assembly, where his government plans to defend its migration policy following the Ceuta crisis and promote multilateralism and Spain’s economic model. Before the trip, Sánchez unveiled IA360, a plan for what he called the responsible deployment of artificial intelligence. Its four pillars include sustainable computing infrastructure, technology talent, AI governance and a new social contract on the effects of AI at work; the government will convene employers and unions from October. Sánchez argued that AI cannot be left to self-regulation and called for global rules to address risks including deepfakes, mental-health harms, monopoly power and intellectual-property theft.
stories.headline: Sánchez takes migration policy and AI regulation agenda to the UN amid mounting domestic tensions

stories.body: Former Valencian regional president Carlos Mazón largely declined to answer questions in a congressional inquiry into the handling of the October 2024 floods, citing his status in the related judicial investigation and saying he should make no public statements until it is complete. He pointed to a regional high-court ruling that rejected his indictment and said he now had full access to the case file. Mazón did say that he was not directing the emergency response when he arrived at the Cecopi coordination center after 8 p.m., shortly after the emergency alert was issued. The inquiry concerns a disaster in which 232 people died in Valencia province.
stories.headline: Carlos Mazón declines to answer most questions in Congress over his handling of the Valencia floods

stories.body: Barcelona’s La Mercè festival will run from September 23 to 27, bringing more than 100 free concerts, street arts, popular culture and events to all 10 city districts. Shanghai is this year’s guest city, while new venues include Plaça de les Glòries and the program includes 109 concerts, 170 street-art performances, castellers, correfocs, parades, museum open days and drone and fireworks displays. The festival will close on September 27 with the Piromusical, which is moving to the seafront because of construction at Montjuïc.
stories.headline: Barcelona prepares for La Mercè, with five days of concerts, culture, drones and fireworks

stories.body: Barcelona’s annual La Mercè Piromusical will be held on Nova Icària beach at 10 p.m. on Sunday, September 27, rather than on Avinguda de la Reina Maria Cristina beside Montjuïc’s Magic Fountain. The relocation is due to major works at the Fira de Barcelona’s Montjuïc site, with the wider Bogatell and Nova Icària seafront expected to give spectators more room. Josep Montero of Oques Grasses will select the music for the approximately 30-minute fireworks-and-sound finale.
stories.headline: La Mercè’s closing piromusical moves to Barcelona’s Nova Icària beach because of works at Montjuïc

stories.body: Barcelona’s public transport operator TMB faces a difficult week as bus drivers plan a seven-hour stoppage on Tuesday so workers can attend a general assembly amid stalled collective-agreement negotiations. Employees on the Montjuïc cable car have also called two-hour strikes on September 24 and 26, during La Mercè, and on October 11. The cable-car workers say negotiations that began early this year have failed to address precarious conditions, work-life balance and other demands for improved labor conditions.
stories.headline: TMB faces a dual strike as cable-car workers join Barcelona bus drivers

stories.body: Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni has urged major cities to create an international alliance on affordable housing, backing an idea associated with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani during the Urban20 summit in New York. Collboni said cities need to share solutions and coordinate against global forces such as speculative investment funds and short-term rental platforms. He cited Barcelona data showing that the share of household income needed for housing rose from 23% in 2014 to 33% in 2024, while rents rose 78% and sale prices 58%; the proposed alliance’s first working meeting is planned for the HOWS Barcelona housing congress in November.
stories.headline: Barcelona mayor Jaume Collboni calls for an international alliance to expand affordable housing
